newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil-Steady and dull, China still inactive.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil-Steady and dull, China still inactive.

text.p: The high sulphur fuel oil market were steady with talk focus on spreads between 180-cst and 380-cst while most Chinese players were still taking a backseat and some gradually returning after the Lunar New Year holidays, traders said.
The spreads between 180-cst and 380-cst, which was once as high as $6-$7 per tonne on Tuesday, narrowed down slightly to $5 in late Wednesday trade but buying interest was still thin.

"I don't see much buying interest today, partly because China is still on holiday and partly because there are still quite enough stocks," said one trader, noting several offers from European and U.S. majors emerged with no takers.
As China has covered its positions throughout February, most traders did not expect Chinese buyers to be active.
Imports are likely to pick up later this month but trades are expected to be slow, traders said.
Supplies and demands patterns are largely unchanged in South Korea, Japan and China, similar to fundamentals early this week, traders said.
One trader said he expected China to start looking for cargoes from around February 24.
"But if China does not buy, which is possible, prices may go down further," the trader said.
Poor bunker demand has also placed pressure on prices. Bunker 180-cst was quoted at $99-$102 and 380-cst was at $93-$97.
No deals were done as most shipowners were waiting for prices to fall further in the near term.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
